geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Cut a rectangle on its diagonal, then split any triangle along an altitude.

Goal: I can derive triangle area from rectangles: a right triangle is half a rectangle, and any triangle is a sum or difference of right triangles.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Area of a triangle = (1/2) base times height, A = (1/2)bh. The height is the length of the altitude, the perpendicular segment from the opposite vertex to the line containing the base.

A right triangle is half of a rectangle cut along its diagonal. Any triangle splits along an altitude into two right triangles whose areas add (altitude inside), or is the difference of two right triangles (altitude outside, for an obtuse triangle). Either way the area is (1/2)bh.

Shearing keeps area: slide the top vertex along a line parallel to the base, and the base and height stay the same.

slides.html:
Shear a triangle along its base; area stays fixed.

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.

slides.html: An obtuse triangle has base 8 and the altitude to it, drawn outside the triangle, is 5. Find its area.
